content: Community health teams are actively conducting campaigns to raise awareness about polio and to promote immunization efforts. To develop this guideline, the World Health Organization (WHO) organized a public hearing and brought together a diverse group of experts, government representatives, stakeholders, partners, and community health workers. This group, known as the guideline development group, was supported by an internal steering group and an external peer review group. The content of the guideline was meticulously informed by systematic reviews of available evidence and a survey capturing stakeholder perceptions. WHO extends its gratitude to all contributors, whose names are listed in the full document. A social mobilizer engages with the community during a yellow fever vaccination campaign to ensure effective communication and participation. For policy dialogue or technical support related to the planning, implementation, or evaluation of community health worker (CHW) programs, you are encouraged to contact WHO. Share your experiences and insights through the CHW Hub, which is part of the Global Health Workforce Network. Lead the way by joining the list of countries that have committed to implementing these guidelines. Become a champion for community health initiatives.
